segments.t: Back at Joon-mo's apartment, Ye-jin scolds him for not properly breaking up with his girlfriend. Listen for "seon", meaning 'line', and "geutda", 'to draw', as she tells him to draw a clear line.
아니, 근데 앞으로 내 인생에 어떤 여자가 등장할지 모르는 이 상황에,
자기 입으로는 또 싫은 얘기 하기 싫어서
야, 이별에도 예의라는 게 있는 법이에요.
Let's unpack these lines to learn how to argue like an old friend.
Ye-jin starts her scolding with a sigh. She says "anida sipeumyeon", meaning 'if you think it is not'.
She tells him to draw a line. She uses "hwaksilhage", 'clearly', and the verb "geueoyaji", 'should draw'.
아니, 근데 앞으로 내 인생에 어떤 여자가 등장할지 모르는 이 상황에,
Joon-mo protests. He talks about "nae insaeng", 'my life', and "eotteon yeojaga", 'which woman'.
He hesitates about drawing a line. He says "geureoke", 'like that', and "geunneundaneun ge", 'the act of drawing'.
He finally gives in. He says "arasseo", 'I understand', and "yegihalge", 'I will tell her'.
Ye-jin is not done. She says "neo gateun nomi", 'a guy like you', and "jeil nappa", 'is the worst'.
자기 입으로는 또 싫은 얘기 하기 싫어서
She calls out his cowardice. She uses "jagi iburoneun", 'with your own mouth', and "sireun yegi", 'words you hate'.
She points out he makes others do the dirty work. She says "namhante", 'to others', and "tteoneomgigo", 'passing it over'.
야, 이별에도 예의라는 게 있는 법이에요.
She reminds him of basic manners. She uses "ibyeoredo", 'even in breakups', and "yeuiraneun ge", 'a thing called courtesy'.
Joon-mo gets annoyed. He shouts "arattago", 'I said I got it', and asks "manuranya", 'are you my wife'.
He mutters about her nagging. He says "jansorineun", which means 'nagging'. Now let's listen to the whole argument again.
아니, 근데 앞으로 내 인생에 어떤 여자가 등장할지 모르는 이 상황에,
자기 입으로는 또 싫은 얘기 하기 싫어서
야, 이별에도 예의라는 게 있는 법이에요.
You just learned how to complain about bad breakups and nagging! Keep practicing to sound natural.
